description.narrative: The world's energy demand is growing fast because of the population explosion and technological advancements (Pham et al., 2020). The limitation of fossil fuel resources and negative environmental effects need special attention to be paid to the reduction of fossil energy use (Ebhota and Jen, 2020). Alternatively, renewable energy sources should be increased. A renewable energy option is a biogas, and its application is growing fast in many countries. It is primarily composed of methane and carbon dioxide gas, and its production plant, according to the level of technology and economic aspects, is appropriate for farmers of developing countries (Rakotojaona, 2013). In general, wastes from livestock (manure and fodder wastes), plant wastes (straw and forage), and kitchen wastes are suitable types of biomasses for biogas production (Zareei, 2018). The conversion of organic waste, such as livestock manure into biogas, is important for several reasons: the high energy released from biogas, i.e., heating value, that can be directly used as an alternative to fossil fuels (Gregorie et al., 2020). the significant effects of using this technology on the environment and human health through hygienic waste disposal; and the generation of rich fertilizer from sludge(soft slurry). For a long time ago, livestockwastes have been a source of energy and a value-added source for livestock production, in many countries. From an energy point of view, the biogas generated will be used for electricity generation and/or heatgeneration (Moreda, 2016). The CU Team, led by Vannasinh Souvannasouk, has had a critical opportunity from Oxfam, which serves in terms of financial and consultation support (January–June2022), to encourage nine household farmers whose livestock feed pigs at the household level in Sanasomboun district to have biogas energy on average of 90–120 m3/month (biogas use 4 hours per day). The model can be used to identify the appropriate locations for the construction of biogas production plants. As a result,the CU Team would like to contribute 10 fixed-dome biogas digesters as a new model for 10 districts in Champasack Province in order to be inspired by the visits of other owners and to benefit other rural households in different districts for the project implementation aimed at addressing environmental problem solutions and providing knowledge transfer to local workers on how technology adaptation can lead to better environmental conditions

The University was established according to the Prime Minister's Decree No. 214/Nya, dated 28/11/2002 In accordance with the education strategy plan of the Ministry of Education and Sports aimed at strengthening higher education to meet the demands of socio-economic development, Champasak National University was established according to Prime Minister's Decree No. 214/Nya, dated 28/11/2002 and was renamed Champasak University according to Prime Minister's Decree No. 35/Nya, dated 07/05/2004. After that,the leadership teamat various levels along with the staff, teachers focused all their wisdom in the development to make this university grow day by day.
The vision is to develop Champasak University into a center for education, scientific research andquality technical services, a green institution and connected to the environment in the south of Lao PDR, regionally and internationally.
